findings.issue: depends_on is [] (correct for the smithery.yaml file authoring + DNS update steps), but the Details section explicitly notes that the Smithery submission step (step 7) only works once Wave 1 + Task 4a (file 5.md) are deployed. The smoke gate `curl https://mcp.mnemonik.xyz/health` will return 502 until then. The author chose to keep depends_on=[] and document the soft dependency in prose — this is a deliberate trade-off, but it complicates wave orchestration if a runner kicks step 7 before Wave 1 ships.
findings.fix: Optional. Either (a) leave as-is and rely on the prose note, or (b) split this task into '6a: smithery.yaml + DNS + nginx + cert (depends_on: [])' and '6b: Smithery submission (depends_on: [1, 5])'. The current single-task structure is acceptable for a manual-coordinated infra task.

findings.issue: Task implements 12 integration tests. Tech-spec Implementation Tasks line 426 says '7 integration tests' but tech-spec Acceptance Criteria line 345 enumerates exactly the 12 files listed in this task. The task correctly follows the AC enumeration (the canonical list); the '7' figure in line 426 is a stale tech-spec inconsistency.
findings.fix: No change needed in the task. Note for the spec author: update tech-spec Implementation Tasks line 426 from '7 integration tests' to '12 integration tests' so the tech-spec is internally consistent.

findings.issue: The smoke checklist adds step 3 ('Keypair backup download') and step 10 ('Cross-device flow') that are not explicitly listed in tech-spec line 434 ('fresh-browser onboarding, keypair gen, install deeplink, OAuth approve, sign_memory, switch to second browser/tool, recall'). Both extensions are well-grounded in user-spec Сценарий 1 (lines 145, 148: backup-JSON + cross-device flow) and user-spec R2 (line 95: localStorage keypair loss mitigation), so they are legitimate carry-forward from the user-spec rather than scope creep.
findings.fix: No change needed — the extension makes the checklist a stronger gate. Optionally, the task could note 'extends tech-spec checklist scope to cover user-spec Сценарий 1 backup + cross-device leg'.

findings.issue: AC includes 'File length is between 80 and 120 lines (documentation density target — concise but unambiguous)'. This is a stylistic constraint rather than a behavioral acceptance criterion; it could end up driving the author to compress legitimate content or pad short content to hit the range.
findings.fix: Optional. Consider rewording as 'File is concise — targets ~100 lines, accepted in the 80-150 range' or drop the line-count AC entirely and rely on the Verify-user gate (a non-author runs the checklist end-to-end without ambiguity).

findings.issue: Smoke step uses `curl -fsS http://localhost:5173/...` to probe Vite dev-server routes. SPA dev servers always return 200 on any path (because the router is client-side); the curl loop verifies the server is up but does not actually exercise the React routes. The 'open in browser' instruction below it is the real check.
findings.fix: Either (a) drop the curl loop and lean entirely on the manual browser walk-through, or (b) keep the curl loop as a 'server-up' liveness check and add an explicit note that route content verification is browser-only.
